title: Pixel fishing minigame (8-sound sprite)
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 192,000 samples (4.0 s at 30 fps = 120 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A 4.0-second sprite of eight soft synthesized pixel-game sounds for a fishing/timing minigame, each starting exactly on frames 0, 15, 30, ..., 105 and silent before the next: 1 cast (short rising square sweep 300→900 Hz + noise swish 120 ms), 2 bobber plop (sine bubble 500→1200 Hz, 50 ms), 3 waiting tick (tiny 2 kHz triangle blip), 4 bite! (two quick pulse notes D6-G6, bright), 5 reel tick (three 3 kHz clicks 40 ms apart), 6 perfect-timing hit (G major triad arpeggio G5-B5-D6-G6 in 30 ms steps, sparkle), 7 miss (a soft descending pulse D5→A4, not comical), 8 catch fanfare (original 4-note pulse figure ending on G6 with a triangle G3 under it). All band-limited, 25%/12.5% duty pulse, gentle 4 kHz low-pass for a cozy feel. Master to -17 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm each slot starts on its frame and is silent (< -60 dBFS) before the next, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.
notes: Eight pixel-game fishing UI slots (cast, plop, tick, bite, reel, perfect, miss, fanfare) with silence between. Mastered to −17 LUFS.
